title: OTWD moderation decision
description: The recorded outcome for a submission, with who or what decided and why. Decisions are appended to the submission log and never edited. An appeal produces a new decision that refers to the earlier one.

outcome.description: approved: applied as submitted. edited_and_approved: applied after a moderator corrected it (amendments lists the corrections). rejected: not applied. needs_info: waiting for the contributor to answer the public note.

routing.description: How routing sent the submission to whoever decided it.

route.description: human_review: a moderator's queue. auto_approval: approved by a routing rule, never used for the always-human list (new sites, closures, merges, safety facts).

always_human.description: True when the submission is on the always-human list.

verdict_ids.description: The verdicts available when the decision was made. A verdict informs a decision and is never one.

code.description: For example confirmed_by_seed_source, duplicate_of_existing_site or copied_text.

public_note.description: The message shown to the contributor and returned to the partner app. Required for rejected and needs_info.

amendments.description: For edited_and_approved: each amendment the moderator made before approving, with the submitted and the applied value.

applied.description: The value as applied, or null when the moderator dropped the field.

merge.description: For an approved request_merge: the surviving site and the sites that now redirect to it.

change_seqs.description: For approved and edited_and_approved: the changes the decision produced. A merge produces one change per site involved.

appeal_of.description: When this decision answers an appeal: the decision appealed against.

allOf.description: Only a moderator may decide a submission on the always-human list, and a routing rule may only approve.

Decider.description: Who or what made the decision. moderator: a person. routing_rule: an automatic approval rule in the fixed routing code, allowed only outside the always-human list. The AI never decides.

moderator_id.description: Moderators are contributors with moderation rights, so they use contributor IDs.
